skill_entry.name: Avoidable per-call work on a per-token, per-layer or spin path
skill_entry.trigger: Both halves. Pattern: an added non-comment line under h/ or src/ (not t/, not src/pos/fake.cpp), outside a constructor, destructor, clear() or function-local `static` initializer, matches: `std::vector`, `.reserve(`, `std::map`, `make_shared`, `make_unique` or `new ` in a function body; `std::memset` or `std::fill` over a whole allocation; `std::sort`; a callback (`*_fn(`) in the innermost of nested loops; a `TRON_ASSERT` whose condition calls a function; a call above an `if` chain in a wait, poll or spin routine; a free (`release_buffer`, `free_`, `evict`, `deallocate`) conditioned only on a counter reaching zero. Path: the function, or one caller up, sits in a spin, layer or token-job loop, `poll_completions`, a wait routine, or is the batched sibling of a singleton (`xfer_gof` -> `xfer_gofs`).
skill_entry.procedure: 1. List pattern hits in added h/ and src/ lines with enclosing functions. 2. Grep callers one level up; classify by loop: spin, per-layer, per-token, completion poll, wait routine, once per forward, startup. Keep the first five, and a once-per-forward function whose BASE lines allocated nothing. 3. Count calls from loop bounds and constants, with a unit; layer count from the named model; no time conversion. 4. Open the singleton sibling or replaced BASE lines; record how they avoided the work. 5. Per pattern: container before the empty check; bytes the loops overwrite; emittable order; callback copies or returns a pointer; branch skipping the value; same assert on every entry path; rebuild then resubmit. 6. Report count, sibling fact, remedy.
skill_entry.question: Does this function, on a path the forward runs per token, per layer, per spin iteration or per DMA completion, do work on every call that the sibling or the replaced lines at BASE did not do (allocate, zero, sort, re-gather, re-assert, rebuild), and does the common case need it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Code run once per request or shard backfill, at startup, in a constructor, clear() or teardown. Test code under t/ and src/pos/fake.cpp. A comment line, a `std::function` member declaration, a trace event or counter (3350412400; the author dropped the comment lines, kept the event). A `static const` initializer reported as per-call work: state the real cost (one init plus a guard check). A container sized by dequeued work after the empty check, the feature's own output buffer, or a sort of queued elements (gof_rodeo_impl_batch at 442ed0dd1a: duplication comment 3907214892, never cost). A free whose risk is a live DMA (buffer-lifetime check). Reported TPS or TTFT numbers, benchmark method, kernel arithmetic. Never demand a measurement; label a slowdown a hypothesis.
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<fn>` (<file:line>) runs <count with unit> per <prefill of N tokens (M layers, model X) | decode token per worker | spin iteration> and <allocates | zeroes <bytes> | sorts | calls `<callback>` <k>x | re-asserts `<cond>`> on every call, where <sibling | the replaced code at BASE> (<file:line>) <uses a fixed array | zeroes only padding | is sorted by construction | gathers once per (pos, head) | asserts once | try_dequeues with zero allocation>. So <consequence with the count>. <seems like we should <remedy>? | this is maybe a nit... but should we check the `<cheap case>` first?>
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit for one misplaced computation in a wait routine ('this is maybe a nit... but it seems like we should check for the `else if (0 == wait_cycles)` case first?', 3350064944; the author accepted at 3350409050; Bill replied that ns_to_cycles could be made cheap, 3351684377, and landed that in PR #2915, commit 2ed902167b, merged 2026-06-05 as 1f68af6047; the branch order at b8739108f7:113/:118 never changed). normal, as a statement with the computed count and the sibling named, for allocation before the empty check, whole-buffer zeroing the loops overwrite, a sort the emission order makes unnecessary, or a repeated gather on a prefill or decode path ('xfer_gofs does some avoidable per-call work on the prefill critical path', 3907183627; 'Two decode-path costs in the drain helpers', 3907185740; the author changed all of them at head 7f80aa17da). minor and not blocking for an eviction or rebuild pattern, as a conversation comment posted with the APPROVED review ('I'm always concerned with performance ... Maybe it won't materialize', 4674512577). Since 2026-03 (first 3002297607 on PR 2233, 2026-03-27) he sometimes has an AI assistant word the concern and pastes it; on PR 4128 the pasted form is conversation comment 5498556672, posted five minutes before the inline comments, and the author's fix commit f0467262cb cites that comment by URL; treat a pasted block as attributed material.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: HEAD is the review commit, confirmed by the comment's cited line numbers, not the API commit field (GitHub moves it to the PR head when the line still applies). If HEAD is not in the worktree (a force-pushed merge commit such as 442ed0dd1a), read it through `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/compare/BASE...HEAD` and `contents/<file>?ref=HEAD`. Full file at HEAD (the function and its if/else chain); callers one level up in h/ and src/ (the loop class); other files: the singleton sibling, the removed lines at BASE, the constants in h/pos/config.hpp, h/tron/gof.hpp and h/libpos.hpp, the callback definitions in h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp, h/common/assert.hpp for TRON_ASSERT; the PR body only for the free/rebuild pattern (the workload the body says it optimizes) and for the model name that gives the layer count. No CI and no runtime needed; a trace is optional and never demanded.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: avoidable per-call work on a per-token, per-layer or spin path

Setup. HEAD is the commit of the review, confirmed by the comment's cited line numbers, not the commit field the API shows (GitHub moves `commit_id` to the PR head while the line still applies: 3907183627 shows 7f80aa17da but its lines :37, :256, :278, :333 are 442ed0dd1a lines; `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/comments/<id> --jq '{commit_id,original_commit_id,original_line}'` gives the review commit). BASE = `git -C WT merge-base HEAD $(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha)`; for a merged PR, `merge-base HEAD origin/main` is HEAD itself and the diff is empty (PR 2903: 64ea13a671 vs origin/main gives 0 files; vs base.sha 09d6fce432 the merge-base is 947d045a14, 25 files). If `git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD` fails (a force-pushed merge commit), take the diff from `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/compare/BASE...HEAD` (one `patch` per file, 3 context lines, map hits through the `@@` headers) and each file from `gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw' repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<file>?ref=HEAD`; `gh pr diff N` is the current head only.

1. Pattern hits in production code, comments and hunk headers excluded from the hit list: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@|\+)' | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+\s*(//|\*)' | grep -E '^[0-9]+:(\+\+\+|@@|\+.*(std::vector|\.reserve\(|std::map|std::memset|std::fill|std::sort|make_shared|make_unique|[^a-z_]new |std::function|_fn\(|TRON_ASSERT[A-Z_]*\([^,]*[a-z_0-9]\(|release_buffer|free_|evict|deallocate))'`. A `@@` line is context for mapping, never a hit; count only `+` lines; drop hits in src/pos/fake.cpp and `std::function` member declarations. Enclosing function of a hit at <file>:<L> (the default awk is mawk 1.3.4, which has no interval expressions, so no `{2,4}` inside awk): for a .cpp file `RX='^[a-zA-Z_][^;]*\([^;]*$'`, for a header `RX='^ {2,4}[a-zA-Z_][^;=]*\([^;]*$'`; then `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E "$RX" | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\s*(return|if|for|while|else|switch|TRON_|TRACE_|static_assert|using|namespace|template|//|#|auto |constexpr)' | awk -F: -v L=<L> '$1<=L{l=$0} END{print l}'`. A result whose line is a data member means "not in a function": treat it as the constructor. Verified at 7f80aa17da: gof.cpp:490 -> dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers :438; model.hpp:3001 -> help_drain_gof :2988; model.hpp:3085 -> gof_rodeo_impl_batch :3063.

1b. Pattern (e), a computation above a branch in a wait, poll or spin routine (no step-1 alternative matches it): `git -C WT diff -U1 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | grep -n -A1 -E '^\+\s*(static const |const )?[a-zA-Z_0-9:<>]+ [a-z_0-9]+ = .*[a-z_0-9]\(.*\).*;\s*$' | grep -B1 -E '^[0-9]+-\+?\s*(if|else if) \(' | grep -v '^--$'` lists added assignment-with-call lines directly above an `if`; keep those whose enclosing function matches `wait|poll|spin|monitor|for_event|indefinitely`. On PR 2903 (`gh pr diff 2903`) this gives one hit, mwaitx.cpp:112 `static const uint64_t mwaitx_min_cycles = ns_to_cycles(300) + 300;` above `if (wait_cycles > mwaitx_min_cycles)`; on the PR 4128 head diff it gives 0 hits in h/ and src/. A `static const` line costs one init plus a guard check per call; say so.

2. Callers and loop class: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<fn>\(' HEAD -- h src | grep -v -E '^\S+:\s*//'`. For each caller line open 15 lines above it and classify: spin (`while (.*load(std::memory_order_acquire)`), per-layer (`for (.*layer`), per-token (`for (.*job|token`), completion poll (`poll_completions`), wait routine (`monitor_and_wait|for_event_cycles|indefinitely`), once per forward (`run_forward`, `assemble_attention_plan`, `compute_forward_args`), startup (`driver.cpp` init, `scan(`, `pos_list_devices`, a constructor). Keep functions with at least one caller in the first five classes. Keep a once-per-forward function only when the lines it replaced at BASE (`git -C WT show BASE:<file>`) did the same work on the same queue with zero allocation (wait_for_coop_gof: BASE 9a905763ac model.hpp:2978-2987 `gof_coop_task task; while (gof_coop_queue_.try_dequeue(task))`, listed by Wade inside 3907185740). Drop a hit whose enclosing function is a constructor, a destructor, clear(), a function-local `static` initializer, or whose only production callers are startup or t/; record each drop with the caller line. A batched sibling has no loop class of its own: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<stem>s?\(|<stem>_batch\(' HEAD -- h src`; state the count premise explicitly ("one call per coalescence window per layer when every window batches fully; xfer_gofs's own TRON_ASSERT at gof.cpp:229-231 bounds a batch to one window").

3. Count: `git -C WT grep -n -E '(hwkv_coalesce_tokens|gof_tokens|hwkv_tok_per_page|HWCACHEBLOCK_BYTES|FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE|HW_MAX_KV_HEADS|HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE|HWBLOCK_POSITIONS|VBLOCK_ROWS_PER_FETCHER|VBLOCK_CELL_STRIDE_BF16|POS_DATA_SIZE)\s*=' HEAD -- h`. The layer count is a model parameter, not a header constant: take it from the model the PR body or config/test-benchmarks.json names and write "36 layers (model X)"; with no model named, give the count per layer and say so. Write calls per forward = (tokens / window tokens) x layers, allocations per spin iteration x workers x layers, gather calls per GOF = FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE x gof_tokens x n_kv_heads, bytes per window = coalesce_gofs x (HWCACHEBLOCK_BYTES + FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE x pchannel_stride x POS_DATA_SIZE), each with its unit. No time conversion.

4. Sibling: `git -C WT show BASE:<file> | sed -n '<start>,<end>p'` for the replaced lines, or the singleton function at HEAD; grep its storage: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E 'std::array|[a-z_]+\[[0-9A-Z_]+\];|std::fill|std::sort|<callback>\('`. If neither a singleton sibling nor the replaced BASE lines avoid the work, and the enclosing function or its caller already built the same container kind per call at BASE, there is no finding under patterns (a)-(d) and (f); write the fact and stop (silent PR 4353 split_sections_by_query: finish_sw_plan already took std::vector parameters at BASE). Patterns (e) and (g) need no sibling.

5. Per pattern. (a) container before the empty check: does `reserve(` or the constructor precede the first `try_dequeue` / `empty()`? Is the size bounded by a constexpr (`std::max(`, `coalesce_gofs`)? Fire only when the container precedes the empty check or the singleton sibling keeps the same data in a fixed array. (b) zeroing: count the loop ranges below against the allocation size in the common geometry. (c) sort: list the emission order of the push_back loops and the comparator keys; fire only when the keys are known at push time and the loops could emit in comparator order; a sort of elements received from a queue or a tree walk is not a finding. (d) nested callback: `grep -n -E '<callback>\('` inside the function; note which loop index its arguments use; compute calls per element versus the sibling; then open the definition `git -C WT grep -n -E '<callback>\s*=' HEAD -- h src` (page_info lambdas live in h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp): a body that copies into a buffer (`get_v(..., dest)` into a captured `v_buf`, full.hpp:2506-2513 at 442ed0dd1a) is a gather and counts per call; a body that returns a pointer (`k(...).data`) is not, and the repeated call is at most a nit; record the `#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE` variant read. (e) computation before a branch: print the `if` / `else if` chain after the added line; name the branch that does not use the value; `git -C WT grep -n -E '<fn>\([^,]+, 0,' HEAD -- h src` for callers that take it; mark `static const` initializers. (f) duplicated assert: `git -C WT grep -n -F '<condition text>' HEAD -- h src` lists both copies directly (model.hpp:3027 fire_gof_rodeo and :3114 gof_rodeo_impl_batch at 442ed0dd1a; a sibling callee, not a caller); then list every entry into the second assert's function (`git grep -n '<fn>('`) and report the duplicate only for paths that pass both (fire_gof_rodeo_batch :3041-3048 calls fire_gof_rodeo per task only for size 1; gof_rodeo_impl :3060-3062 enters impl_batch directly). `git -C WT show HEAD:h/common/assert.hpp | grep -n -E 'NDEBUG|define TRON_ASSERT'` (:3-4 undef NDEBUG, :69 define; the assert runs in release). (g) free on counter zero: print the free function; `git -C WT grep -n -E 'prepare_for_dma\(|reacquire|populate\(' HEAD -- h src` for the rebuild path; `git -C WT grep -n -E 'xfer_gof\(|backfill_shard|gof_rodeo_impl' HEAD -- h src` for every submit site; ask whether two submissions of the same object follow each other (fanout loop, speculation, retry). A free whose risk is a DMA still reading the buffer belongs to the buffer-lifetime check; here report only the rebuild count.

6. Report: function, HEAD line, the count with unit, the sibling or BASE line that already avoids the work, the remedy. Nit for one misplaced computation; normal statement for allocation before the empty check, overwritten zeroing, an avoidable sort or a repeated gather on a prefill or decode path; minor and not blocking, as a conversation comment, for an eviction or rebuild pattern. A duplicated statement off the five hot-path loop classes belongs to the redundant-code check.

On PR 4128 at the review commit 442ed0dd1a (a merge of main into the branch; BASE 9a905763ac is its second parent; the commit is on GitHub only, read through gh api compare and contents?ref=; the API lists 3907183627 under 7f80aa17da but its cited lines are 442ed0dd1a lines): step 1 over the compare patches gives 36 code hits, all of Wade's lines among them. h/tron/models/model.hpp:2973-2974 `std::vector<gof_coop_task> tasks; tasks.reserve(task_budget);` precede the first `try_dequeue` and `if (tasks.empty()) return;` (:2977-2978, help_drain_gof); :2993-2994 the same shape in wait_for_coop_gof (Wade wrote :2993; caller run_forward :1813, once per forward, BASE :2978-2987 allocated nothing); callers of help_drain_gof: self_attention.hpp:793 (begin_attention_job) and :904-908 inside `while (hw_q_released_layer.load(std::memory_order_acquire) <` (spin), so one malloc per spin iteration per worker per layer per decode token; src/tron/gof.cpp:37 `std::memset(data, 0, size)` on the whole batch allocation (8 GOFs x (8192 B K + 32 x 256 B V) = 128 KiB per window at hwkv_coalesce_tokens = 32, config.hpp:99; the K loop :305-322 and the V loop :325-343 write every byte at 8 heads x 128 head size); heap vectors at gof.cpp:255-256, :289, :346-349 where the singleton xfer_gof uses `hbm_address_t bases[36]` and three more fixed arrays at :194-197 and `specs[36]` at :186; `std::sort(pieces...)` at :278 after gi-major push_back loops at :260-276 with keys (kind, fetcher, base) known at push time; `gof_pages[pos].v_head_fn(layer, head)` at :333 inside the (piece, pos, head) loops with arguments independent of `piece.fetcher`, 32 x 4 x 8 = 1024 calls per GOF against 32 in gof::populate :384-388, and the v_head_fn body (full.hpp:2506-2513) copies through get_v into a captured v_buf while k_head_fn :312 returns a pointer; model.hpp:3023-3030 (fire_gof_rodeo) and :3110-3116 (gof_rodeo_impl_batch) assert the same `kv_complete_fn(layer)` text. Count: 4096 tokens / 32 tokens per window = 128 windows x 36 layers (the model Wade assumed; no header holds 36) = 4608 xfer_gofs calls per prefill. Not findings at the same commit: gof_rodeo_impl_batch `std::vector<prepared_xfer> prepared; prepared.reserve(tasks.size())` :3090-3091 (after the drain helper's empty check), its std::sort :3136 (elements from the queue) and the four per-shard-group vectors :3167-3174, backfill_shard :429/:471/:498-505 (once per shard backfill), `std::make_shared<gof_dma_batch>` :287 (the DMA source buffer), k_head_fn :312 (pointer); Wade's comment on that block, 3907214892, is about four copies, not cost. Head 7f80aa17da (BASE 1279137d25, merge-base with origin/main; step 1 gives 32 hits in 5 files): gof.cpp:248-252 `std::array<..., max_specs>`, :279-283 zeroing only when heads or head size are below the baked geometry (std::fill on padded slots :294, :300, :323), comment :244-247 "without a sort or generic coalescing pass"; model.hpp:3000-3001 `std::array<gof_coop_task, drain_capacity> tasks; if (!gof_coop_queue_.try_dequeue(tasks[0])) return;`, :3019-3020 wait_for_coop_gof std::array<gof_coop_task, coalesce_gofs>; one assert left at :3085-3091; gof.cpp:490 is the only xfer_gofs call and sits inside dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers (:438), called from backfill_shard (gof.cpp:557) and gof_rodeo_impl_batch (model.hpp:3111), so at the head the batched transfer also runs on the decode path; dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers std::sort :442 and vectors :476-483 and model.hpp:3065-3066 remain and are not findings under step 5.

On PR 2903: src/system/mwaitx.cpp:112 `static const uint64_t mwaitx_min_cycles = ns_to_cycles(300) + 300;` above `if (wait_cycles > mwaitx_min_cycles)` :113 and `else if (0 == wait_cycles)` :118 at both 64ea13a671 and head b8739108f7; the indefinite caller is `monitor_and_wait(trigger, 0, condition)` at :186 (indefinitely); for_event_cycles :178 passes a non-zero wait; h/system/system.hpp:229-232 ns_to_cycles is an inline TRON_ASSERT plus precise_scale, so the per-call cost is the static-init guard, not a `ns_to_cycles` call; branch order unchanged at the merged head; the remedy that landed is a cheaper ns_to_cycles in PR #2915 (2ed902167b, merged 2026-06-05 as 1f68af6047).

On PR 2906 (`gh pr diff 2906`, 1446 lines): step 1 with the comment filter leaves about 7 code hits (release_buffer x4, dma_deallocate, free_staging_if_idle x2; about 20 `// See Note [GOF staging eviction]` lines drop out); at 678f559d5d h/tron/gof.hpp:224-237 free_staging_if_idle releases k and v whenever dma_inflight == 0 and either buffer is allocated; :201-219 prepare_for_dma reacquires and populates (the rebuild); src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp:101-109 calls it on every completed pending_xfer whose decrement reaches zero; submit sites that rebuild then DMA the same gof: model.hpp:1942-1943 (gof_rodeo_impl) and gof.cpp:153-155 (backfill_shard).

Probe record (2026-10-06 silent set, 15 approved-without-text diffs): the step-1 regex hits 1722 (constructor memset and new), 2135 (constructor new, init_clear_kv_hbm from driver.cpp:296 startup loop), 2875 (a vector in a test-only verifier, evict already at BASE, three asserts not duplicated one level up), 3756 (scan() new at startup), 4353 (five vectors in split_sections_by_query, once per forward, finish_sw_plan already built vectors at BASE) and 1739 under the `new ` pattern (a function-local static singleton); the loop-class step, the constructor and static-initializer exclusions and the step-4 no-sibling rule drop every hit; no finding survives.

quotes.quote: xfer_gofs does some avoidable per-call work on the prefill critical path (a 4096-token 36-layer prefill runs this ~4608 times):
quotes.what_it_shows: The normal-severity form: a statement that names the function, the path and the computed call count before the item list.

quotes.quote: gof.cpp:256+ — six heap vectors per call (pieces/specs/bases/fetchers/qdatas/qlens); the sibling xfer_gof uses fixed stack arrays. Sizes are bounded by coalesce_gofs*(1+FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE), so stack arrays work here too.

changes_made: Trigger: pattern list and step-1 regex now agree (both carry std::map, make_unique and `new `); added the exclusions for comment lines, constructor and destructor bodies, clear(), function-local `static` initializers, src/pos/fake.cpp and std::function member declarations (precision P1, P3, P8; executability P5, P11).

Trigger and procedure step 2: 'once per forward' resolved against both lenses by re-reading 3907185740 and BASE 9a905763ac model.hpp:2978-2987. Wade listed wait_for_coop_gof (called once per forward from run_forward :1813) because the replaced code try_dequeued with zero allocation; silent PR 4353's planner already built vectors at BASE. Rule adopted: a once-per-forward function fires only when its replaced BASE lines did the same work without allocation; the do-not-fire list no longer names 'once per forward' (precision P2 fix taken in part, executability P7/F7 taken).

Procedure step 1: replaced the mawk-incompatible awk enclosing-function command with the grep plus awk form; verified on this host (mawk 1.3.4, no gawk) at 7f80aa17da for gof.cpp:490, model.hpp:3001 and :3085 (executability P1/F1).

Procedure step 1b added for pattern (e) with a corrected regex that allows trailing arithmetic after the call; verified: one hit on PR 2903 (mwaitx.cpp:112 above the if chain), zero hits on the PR 4128 head diff (precision P4, executability P4/F4; the refuter's F4 regex required `);` at line end and missed the member, fixed here).
